officialSourcePolicyCandidate.title: Braille Music — Music Committee position statement
officialSourcePolicyCandidate.policy: Use ICEB's current position statement as the authority for international source precedence. ICEB identifies Music Braille Code 2015 as the most up-to-date resource and the 1996 New International Manual as a complementary international reference.

officialSourcePolicyCandidate.title: Music Braille Code, 2015
officialSourcePolicyCandidate.policy: Primary rule/codebook source for Phase 14. Store normalized rule facts and provenance in the repository; do not vendor or alter the full copyrighted codebook. BANA states the publication may be duplicated but not altered.

officialSourcePolicyCandidate.title: Standard MIDI Files
officialSourcePolicyCandidate.policy: Primary source for the MIDI input container/event model. The official page confirms time-stamped MIDI streams, track/sequence structure, tempo and time-signature information.

officialSourcePolicyCandidate.title: Browsers and webview controls used by Office Add-ins
officialSourcePolicyCandidate.policy: Windows Office Add-ins run in Microsoft Edge WebView2 on supported Office versions. Local file-picker behavior must still be acceptance-tested in the actual Word Desktop preview.

officialSourcePolicyCandidate.title: Word add-in tutorial / Word.Range.insertText
officialSourcePolicyCandidate.policy: Use the existing WordApi 1.1 selection insertion path. Phase 14 must not add an Excel or PowerPoint music execution path.

directOrStructurallyAvailable.phase14Use: YES as source structure, NOT automatically notation voices

directOrStructurallyAvailable.basis: SMF tempo meta information when present
SMF time-signature meta information when present
SMF key-signature meta event when present

requiresDeterministicNotationPolicy.reason: Performed MIDI timing can contain expressive offsets and does not itself guarantee exact engraved note values.
Rests are derived from gaps in a notation timeline rather than explicit note events.
Pitch octave is available, but Music Braille octave signs are context-sensitive rather than a direct per-note dump.
MIDI note number preserves chromatic pitch but not original enharmonic spelling such as C-sharp versus D-flat.
MIDI tracks/channels are not equivalent to engraved voices.
Requires time-signature/timeline interpretation and a defined fallback when source metadata is absent.

notFaithfullyRecoverableByDefault: explicit print dynamics markings from velocity alone
explicit articulation marks from duration alone
editorial markings not encoded in MIDI

preferred.musicEngine: new platform-agnostic music package/module, independent of Office
preferred.sdkFacade: expose Music Braille through the existing public SDK boundary so Microsoft365 continues to depend on public SDK rather than a private Core/music implementation

candidateModuleBoundary.invariant: Office -> public SDK -> music engine; never Office -> private music engine internals.
candidateModuleBoundary.futureProofing: A future MusicXML adapter must terminate at the same neutral semantic music model and must not require a rewrite of the Braille encoder.

pipeline: quantize notation timeline under explicit policy
resolve pitch spelling under explicit policy
insert successful output at current Word selection

ui.insertRule: Insert only a successful generated preview at the current Word selection/cursor; no Excel/PowerPoint music action.

enable: track/part separation where source structure is explicit
key signature when explicitly present and parser support is verified

diagnosticFamiliesToFreezeNext: track/channel treated as source part rather than notation voice
notation detail omitted because MIDI does not preserve it

openContractDecisions.question: Freeze the exact Standard MIDI File subset accepted by the first implementation (for example SMF types/time division).
openContractDecisions.reason: The parser contract must fail explicitly on unsupported containers/timing models rather than silently misread them.

openContractDecisions.question: Freeze deterministic duration/rest quantization tolerances and supported rhythmic values.
openContractDecisions.reason: Performance timing is not identical to engraved notation.

openContractDecisions.question: Freeze canonical enharmonic spelling policy and its use of an explicit MIDI key-signature event when available.
openContractDecisions.reason: MIDI note number does not preserve original spelling.

openContractDecisions.question: Freeze chord/polyphony/part handling and explicitly avoid equating MIDI tracks/channels with notation voices.
openContractDecisions.reason: Braille Music representation depends on musical structure, not merely event ordering.

openContractDecisions.question: Freeze behavior when tempo, time signature, or key signature metadata is absent.
openContractDecisions.reason: Phase 14 must distinguish defaults required for timeline calculation from claims that the source explicitly encoded a notation marking.

openContractDecisions.question: Acceptance-test local .mid/.midi selection in the actual Windows Word Desktop WebView2 task pane.
openContractDecisions.reason: The architecture permits a browser file input, but Phase 14 must prove the UX in the exact supported host before closure.

next: Materialize Phase 14.2b architecture/source-policy/semantic/UI contract only after reviewing this audit. Do not implement a MIDI parser or Music Braille encoder before the contract is frozen.
